```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.width = 7, fig.height = 4)
```

This vignette reproduces all estimates, bounds, thresholds, implied
comparisons, and bootstrap confidence intervals reported in the examples
section of Locher, Richardson, and Stensrud (2026).

## Data

With a binary instrument $Z$, treatment $A$, and outcome $Y$, the observed
data are fully summarised by the counts of the eight combinations of
$(Z, A, Y)$. The counts below are those reported in the appendix of the
manuscript.

* **Example 1** (Bakker et al., 2019): $Z$ indicates assignment to the group
  invited to supplemental MRI screening, $A$ participation in MRI screening,
  and $Y$ a diagnosis of interval breast cancer. The counts are taken from
  the published trial results.
* **Example 2** (Finkelstein et al., 2012): $Z$ indicates selection in the
  Oregon Health Insurance Experiment lottery, $A$ enrollment in Medicaid, and
  $Y$ any primary care visit in the previous 12 months, as reported by
  respondents to the 12-month survey. The counts are derived from the public
  use data of the experiment (NBER, <https://doi.org/10.60592/rx0z-sp89>).

```{r data}
library(ivate)

counts <- data.frame(
  z         = rep(0:1, each = 4),
  a         = rep(rep(0:1, each = 2), times = 2),
  y         = rep(0:1, times = 4),
  example_1 = c(32151, 161, 0, 0, 3262, 16, 4779, 4),
  example_2 = c(4717, 5572, 292, 1230, 2971, 3745, 1315, 3650)
)
counts

# One row per individual
bakker <- expand_counts(counts[, c("z", "a", "y", "example_1")], count = "example_1")
oregon <- expand_counts(counts[, c("z", "a", "y", "example_2")], count = "example_2")
c(example_1 = nrow(bakker), example_2 = nrow(oregon))
```

All confidence intervals are percentile intervals from 1000 bootstrap
replicates. As in the manuscript, the seed is reset to the same value before
every analysis.

```{r settings}
n_boot <- 1000
seed   <- 2026
```

## Example 1: supplemental MRI screening for breast cancer

Non-compliance is one-sided: no women in the control group underwent MRI
screening, so there are no always-takers and $\theta_N^{(1)}$ is the only
sensitivity parameter. The decision criterion is $\Psi_{ATE} < 0$.

**LATE and unrestricted bounds.** Without restrictions, the bounds coincide
with the Balke-Pearl bounds.

```{r bakker-bounds}
set.seed(seed)
bounds_b <- ate_bounds(bakker, y ~ a | z, n_boot = n_boot)
bounds_b
```

**Decomposition.** The identified quantities entering the decomposition of
the ATE:

```{r bakker-identified}
bounds_b$identified[, c("quantity", "estimate", "ci_lower", "ci_upper")]
```

**Threshold and implied comparisons.** The criterion holds if and only if
$\theta_N^{(1)}$ lies below the threshold. At the threshold, the output
reports the implied effect and risk ratio among never-takers and the implied
outcome heterogeneity between never-takers and compliers under treatment,
next to the observed heterogeneity under no treatment ($\mu_N^{(0)} -
\mu_C^{(0)}$; the manuscript reports its negative, $\mu_C^{(0)} -
\mu_N^{(0)}$).

```{r bakker-sensitivity}
set.seed(seed)
sens_b <- ate_sensitivity(bakker, y ~ a | z, direction = "less", n_boot = n_boot)
sens_b
plot_comparisons(sens_b)
```

The implied comparisons with confidence intervals for both the implied
values and the identified benchmarks:

```{r bakker-implied}
sens_b$implied[, c("comparison", "implied_value", "implied_ci_lower", "implied_ci_upper",
                   "benchmark_value", "benchmark_ci_lower", "benchmark_ci_upper")]
```

**Improved bounds.** Assuming that MRI screening increases cancer incidence
among never-takers by at most a factor of 1.2:

```{r bakker-ratio}
set.seed(seed)
bounds_b_rr <- ate_bounds(bakker, y ~ a | z,
                          theta_N1 = restrict_ratio(upper = 1.2), n_boot = n_boot)
bounds_b_rr
```

## Example 2: public health insurance and health care utilization

Non-compliance is two-sided, so both $\theta_A^{(0)}$ and $\theta_N^{(1)}$ are
unidentified. The decision criterion is $\Psi_{ATE} > 0$.

**LATE, unrestricted bounds, and the boundary.** Without a restriction on
either sensitivity parameter, the criterion is characterised by the boundary
$\mathcal{B}$, reported both on the level scale and on the scale of the
implied type-specific effects.

```{r oregon-boundary}
set.seed(seed)
sens_f <- ate_sensitivity(oregon, y ~ a | z, n_boot = n_boot)
sens_f

set.seed(seed)
bounds_f <- ate_bounds(oregon, y ~ a | z, n_boot = n_boot)
bounds_f
```

**Step 1: worst case for $\theta_A^{(0)}$.** Fixing $\theta_A^{(0)} = 1$
yields a threshold for $\theta_N^{(1)}$ and the implied comparisons at that
threshold.

```{r oregon-step1}
set.seed(seed)
step_1 <- ate_sensitivity(oregon, y ~ a | z, theta_A0 = 1, n_boot = n_boot)
step_1
plot_comparisons(step_1)
step_1$implied[, c("comparison", "implied_value", "implied_ci_lower", "implied_ci_upper",
                   "benchmark_value", "benchmark_ci_lower", "benchmark_ci_upper")]

set.seed(seed)
ate_bounds(oregon, y ~ a | z, theta_A0 = 1, n_boot = n_boot)
```

**Step 2: a credible restriction on $\theta_A^{(0)}$.** Assuming a
non-negative treatment effect among always-takers, the least favourable value
is $\theta_A^{(0)} = \mu_A^{(1)}$, re-estimated in every bootstrap replicate.

```{r oregon-step2}
set.seed(seed)
step_2 <- ate_sensitivity(oregon, y ~ a | z,
                          theta_A0 = restrict_effect(lower = 0), n_boot = n_boot)
step_2

set.seed(seed)
ate_bounds(oregon, y ~ a | z, theta_A0 = restrict_effect(lower = 0), n_boot = n_boot)
```

**Improved bounds under stable outcome heterogeneity.** Never-takers and
compliers differ under treatment by at most as much as under no treatment,
$|\theta_N^{(1)} - \mu_C^{(1)}| \le |\mu_N^{(0)} - \mu_C^{(0)}|$, and
analogously for always-takers,
$|\theta_A^{(0)} - \mu_C^{(0)}| \le |\mu_A^{(1)} - \mu_C^{(1)}|$.

```{r oregon-heterogeneity}
set.seed(seed)
ate_bounds(
  oregon, y ~ a | z,
  theta_N1 = restrict_heterogeneity(lower = ~ -abs(mu_N0 - mu_C0), upper = ~ abs(mu_N0 - mu_C0)),
  theta_A0 = restrict_heterogeneity(lower = ~ -abs(mu_A1 - mu_C1), upper = ~ abs(mu_A1 - mu_C1)),
  n_boot = n_boot
)
```

## References

Bakker, M. F., et al. (2019). Supplemental MRI screening for women with
extremely dense breast tissue. *New England Journal of Medicine*, 381(22),
2091--2102.

Finkelstein, A., et al. (2012). The Oregon Health Insurance Experiment:
Evidence from the first year. *The Quarterly Journal of Economics*, 127(3),
1057--1106.

Locher, L., Richardson, T., and Stensrud, M. (2026). Informative inference on
the average treatment effect with instrumental variables.

National Bureau of Economic Research. Oregon Health Insurance Experiment
public use data. <https://doi.org/10.60592/rx0z-sp89>
